findings.suggested_fix:
In MATCHING/1d_for_mlp_tgt.do:81-83 (and analogously in MATCHING/1c_tgt_divided_files.do:111-113), replace from `_ans_cleaned` whenever `!tgt | !name_true_cleaned_exists`:
`replace namefrst_true_cleaned = f_name if !tgt | !name_true_cleaned_exists`
`replace namelast_true_cleaned = l_name if !tgt | !name_true_cleaned_exists`
`replace mi_true_cleaned = mi if !tgt | !name_true_cleaned_exists`
For target records with `name_true_cleaned_exists==1` where only the surname came from the model and `namefrst_ml` was empty (so the first name fell back to `namefrst_ans_cleaned` and lost its middle initial), also restore `replace mi_true_cleaned = mi if tgt & name_true_cleaned_exists==1 & mi_true_cleaned=="" & namefrst_true_cleaned==f_name` (or track first-name model presence separately).
findings.title: Target records without model output lose Ancestry's middle initial and keep double-cleaned fallback names
findings.what_the_code_does: The header at MATCHING/1d_for_mlp_tgt.do:7-9 states that for a target record, `namefrst_true_cleaned`, `namelast_true_cleaned`, and `mi_true_cleaned` are "the model's (Ancestry's where the model gave none), from divided_file1940_true_cleaned_women_added". Lines 81-84 therefore overwrite those variables with `f_name`, `l_name`, and `mi` from `divided_file1940_ans_cleaned_women_added` only `if !tgt`. However, `divided_file1940_true_cleaned_women_added` does not preserve Ancestry's middle initial `mi` (or exact `_ans_cleaned` names) when the model gave none (`name_true_cleaned_exists==0`) or when `namefrst_ml` was empty: MATCHING/1_divide_and_clean_everyoneV5_women_addedV2.do:150 loads `namefrst_ans_cleaned` and `namelast_ans_cleaned` (already cleaned by `abeclean` in MATCHING/0_create_file_for_matching_intgenV4_women_added.do:87, which stripped the second token into `mi` and kept a single-word first name; see LINKAGE/code/01_abe_jw/reference/abeclean.ado:232-241), copies them via Stata variable abbreviation `namefrst_ans`/`namelast_ans` at lines 169-170, and runs `abeclean ..., initial(mi_true_cleaned)` a second time at line 173. Because the middle initial was already removed from `namefrst_ans_cleaned` in step 0, `mi_true_cleaned` is wiped to `""` on fallback records, and non-idempotent `abeclean` mappings alter `f_name`/`l_name` (436 of 1,031,654 men's fallback records in MATCHING/1c_tgt_divided_files.do:129, plus women).
findings.why_it_matters: For the roughly 10% of target records where the model gave no usable transcription (`tgt==1 & name_true_cleaned_exists==0`, plus target records where `namefrst_ml==""` fell back to Ancestry while `namelast_ml_ditto!=""`), `for_mlp1940_tgt.dta` supplies `mi_true_cleaned == ""` instead of Ancestry's middle initial `mi` (and double-`abeclean`ed names on the non-idempotent cases) to IPUMS MLP linking and downstream middle-initial validation.

findings.how_to_check: Run `git grep -n "1d_for_mlp_tgt"` to confirm no script calls `MATCHING/1d_for_mlp_tgt.do`, and inspect `MATCHING/1d_for_mlp_tgt.do:35,76-78` to confirm it requires `tgt_flag1940.dta` to pre-exist without building it or asserting its row count.
findings.suggested_fix: Either build `tgt_flag1940.dta` from `census1940_all_labeled_data.dta` inside `MATCHING/1d_for_mlp_tgt.do` when the file is absent (as `MATCHING/1c_tgt_divided_files.do:51-65` does), or validate `tgt_flag1940.dta` before the loop (`use "`flags'", clear`, `isid id`, `assert tgt==1`, and assert the expected target count from the 122,551,263-record labeled dataset), and wire `1d_for_mlp_tgt.do` into the target-only build driver.
findings.title: 1d_for_mlp_tgt.do depends on a pre-existing tgt_flag1940.dta without building or validating it and has no driver caller
findings.what_the_code_does: `MATCHING/1d_for_mlp_tgt.do:35` executes `confirm file "`flags'""` (`$REP_F/enum_date/DATA/INTERMEDIATE/tgt_flag1940.dta`) and merges it at lines 76-78 with `keep(1 3) keepusing(tgt)` and `replace tgt = 0 if _merge==1`. It does not build `tgt_flag1940.dta` if missing, does not assert the row count or `tgt==1` invariant of `tgt_flag1940.dta` if present, and is not called by any master or driver script (`MATCHING/_tgt_only_run.do`, `MATCHING/_matching_master_dofile.do`, or `replication/run_machineA.do`).
findings.why_it_matters: Running `MATCHING/1d_for_mlp_tgt.do` on a clean environment fails at line 35 with `r(601)` unless `MATCHING/1c_tgt_divided_files.do` has already been run and its intermediate flag file left on disk. Conversely, if a stale `tgt_flag1940.dta` is present on disk from an earlier definition (such as the earlier draft noted at `MATCHING/1c_tgt_divided_files.do:49-50` that used `fs_cells.do`'s human-complete subset), `1d_for_mlp_tgt.do` silently consumes it and builds the 131.9M-row `for_mlp1940_tgt.dta` with the wrong target set.

findings.how_to_check: In `MATCHING/1d_for_mlp_tgt.do`, before `drop _merge` at line 78, accumulate `quietly count if _merge==1` and `quietly count if _merge==1 & name_true_cleaned_exists==1` across the 144 birthplace files to see how many records outside `census1940_all_labeled_data.dta` have model names overwritten with Ancestry names.
findings.suggested_fix: Accumulate and report the count of unmatched divided-file records (`_merge==1`) and the subset with `name_true_cleaned_exists==1` in `MATCHING/1d_for_mlp_tgt.do`'s final summary display, and state explicitly in the paper/slides that target status is defined only on the 122.55M records with non-missing names and ages in both Ancestry and FamilySearch, so the ~9.35M 1940 records missing from FamilySearch retain Ancestry names in the linking pool.
findings.title: The 9.35M divided-file records absent from census1940_all_labeled_data.dta are treated as concordant non-targets in for_mlp1940_tgt.dta
findings.what_the_code_does: `for_mlp1940_tgt.dta` is built from `divided_file1940_{ans,true}_cleaned_women_added` (131,899,064 records; `LINKAGE/DOCUMENTATION.md:49`), which keeps all white and Black 1940 records with `bpl<900` and non-empty Ancestry names (`MATCHING/1_divide_and_clean_everyoneV5_women_addedV2.do:53-55`). `tgt_flag1940.dta` is built from `census1940_all_labeled_data.dta` (122,551,263 records), which required non-empty names and non-missing ages in both Ancestry and FamilySearch (`namelast!="" & namefrst!="" & namefrst_fs!="" & namelast_fs!="" & age!=. & age_fs!=.` at `CODE/clean_FS_and_combineV5_nber.do:225`). At `MATCHING/1d_for_mlp_tgt.do:76-84`, all ~9.35M records in the `_women_added` divided files that do not appear in `census1940_all_labeled_data.dta` (`_merge==1`, including 4,819,575 men noted in `MATCHING/tgt_fallback_diag.do:8`) are assigned `tgt = 0` and forced to keep Ancestry names.
findings.why_it_matters: A record with an Ancestry name that is absent from `census1940_all_labeled_data.dta` because FamilySearch lacked a first name, surname, or age is not a record where the two human transcriptions agreed; it is a record where FamilySearch was incomplete or unlinked. While the evaluation denominator (`linkage_sample1940.dta`) is restricted to `census1940_all_labeled_data.dta`, IPUMS MLP linking runs on the full 131.9M-record pool in `for_mlp1940_tgt.dta`, where reverting model transcriptions on those 9.35M records affects candidate competition and household context without `1d_for_mlp_tgt.do` reporting how many `_merge==1` records had model names replaced.

structured_output.summary: Reviewed the uncommitted working-tree changes centered on MATCHING/1d_for_mlp_tgt.do across all four active dimensions. The script accurately mirrors the 11-variable schema, birthplace code construction, and shard-level 1:1 checks of the original for_mlp1940.dta build, but has one major correctness bug: for target records where the model gave no transcription (name_true_cleaned_exists==0), keeping divided_file1940_true_cleaned_women_added values instead of falling back to _ans_cleaned wipes their middle initial mi_true_cleaned to empty (because 1_divide_and_clean_everyoneV5_women_addedV2.do ran abeclean a second time on already-cleaned namefrst_ans_cleaned from which mi had already been stripped) and retains the 436+ non-idempotent double-abecleaned names. In addition, 1d_for_mlp_tgt.do depends on an unverified pre-existing tgt_flag1940.dta and is not wired into any driver script.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
